findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored unencrypted at rest by default.

findings.issue_category: missing public access block / no explicit ACL
findings.description: No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket and no explicit ACL is set, leaving the bucket without an enforced private-access boundary and relying entirely on AWS account-level defaults.
The bucket stores financial ledger export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving sensitive data unencrypted at rest.
The bucket has versioning and logging configured but no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted at rest.
The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so operational runbook data is stored unencrypted at rest.

findings.issue_category: force_destroy enabled on sensitive bucket without versioning
findings.description: force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be permanently deleted, and combined with the absence of a versioning block, there is no protection against accidental or malicious data loss.

The bucket has force_destroy = true and no versioning configuration block, meaning financial ledger export data can be irrecoverably deleted or overwritten, undermining data integrity expectations for financial records.

The object is uploaded to reports_archive, a bucket without default encryption, and the object resource itself does not specify server-side encryption, so this file (potentially containing vendor PII) is stored in cleartext.
